tasks.title: Fix Map Image Viewport Clipping
tasks.description: Address the issue where the map image is clipped at the bottom of the screen, cutting off turn markers 8, 9, and 10.
tasks.details: Investigate the Board scene's camera or container sizing. Adjust CSS, camera bounds, or container overflow properties to ensure the entire map image, including all turn markers, is fully visible and accessible when scrolling or zooming. Ensure responsive design principles are applied.
tasks.testStrategy: Manually verify the bottom of the map (including turn 8, 9, 10 markers) is accessible after zooming/panning. Implement a Playwright E2E test to verify the map renders at full height and specific elements are visible.

tasks.title: Fix Initial Camera Zoom Level
tasks.description: Correct the Board scene camera to start at the maximum zoomed-out state, displaying the entire map on first load.
tasks.details: Modify the camera initialization logic within the Board scene. Set the initial camera zoom level to the maximum zoom-out value so the entire map fits on screen. Verify and adjust region hit polygon scaling to ensure accuracy at this default zoom level.
tasks.testStrategy: Start a new game and visually verify the entire map is visible without manual panning or zooming. Click various regions to confirm that hit zones are accurate at the default zoom level.

tasks.title: Fix Race & Power HUD Interaction Passthrough
tasks.description: Prevent map interactions (region tooltips, hover, clicks) when the Race & Power selection HUD is open.
tasks.details: Implement a pointer event blocking mechanism for the HUD. This can be achieved by adding a transparent overlay behind the HUD that captures all pointer events, or by dynamically setting `pointer-events: none` on the map container when the HUD is active and `pointer-events: auto` on the HUD itself. Ensure the HUD's z-index is higher than the map.
tasks.testStrategy: Open the Race & Power HUD, hover over HUD options, and verify that no map tooltips appear and no map regions respond to input. Attempt to click on map regions while the HUD is open and confirm no actions are triggered.

tasks.title: Fix Tooltip Zoom Scaling
tasks.description: Ensure tooltips maintain a constant visual size regardless of the camera zoom level.
tasks.details: Refactor the tooltip rendering logic to use screen-space coordinates instead of world-space coordinates. This might involve using CSS `position: fixed` or rendering tooltips on a dedicated UI layer that does not scale with the game world. Adjust tooltip panel dimensions, font size, and positioning to remain constant relative to the viewport.
tasks.testStrategy: Zoom in and out while hovering over various regions. Verify that the tooltip appearance (size, font) remains identical and legible at all zoom levels.

tasks.title: Fix Conquest Cost Calculation and Tooltip
tasks.description: Correctly calculate and display the conquest cost in the tooltip, accounting for all defenders and terrain modifiers.
tasks.details: Update the `calculateConquestCost()` function to accurately compute the cost: 2 (base) + 1 per Mountain token + 1 per Encampment + 1 per Fortress + 1 per Troll's Lair + 1 per Lost Tribe token + 1 per enemy race token present. Integrate this corrected cost into the conquest tooltip display for each region.
tasks.testStrategy: Create test scenarios with regions containing different combinations of defenders and terrain modifiers. Hover over these regions and verify the tooltip displays the correct computed cost. Attempt a conquest with insufficient tokens and confirm it is correctly rejected.

tasks.title: Fix First Conquest Entry Rule Enforcement
tasks.description: Enforce the game rule that a player's first conquest must target a border or coastal region, with exceptions for specific race/power abilities.
tasks.details: Modify the `getLegalActions()` function. During the first conquest of the game (when the player has no occupied regions), filter the returned valid conquest targets to include only regions marked as `isBorder` or `isCoastal`. Implement conditional logic to allow Halflings and Flying powers to bypass this restriction.
tasks.testStrategy: Start a new game and enter the conquest phase. Verify that only border and coastal regions are highlighted as valid first conquest targets, and non-border/non-coastal regions cannot be clicked. Test with Halflings and Flying powers to ensure they can conquer any region.

tasks.title: Fix Decline Flow — Surface Decline Option to Player
tasks.description: Make the 'Decline' option accessible in the UI at the correct phase of the player's turn and ensure it triggers the game engine's decline function.
tasks.details: Implement a 'Decline' button in the player HUD. Control its visibility based on the current game phase (e.g., after ready troops, during or after conquest). On button click, invoke the existing `applyDecline()` engine function. Ensure the UI updates correctly to reflect decline: banner flips to gray, tokens reduce to 1 per region, and the power badge is removed. Handle Spirit and Ghoul exceptions as per game rules.
tasks.testStrategy: Play through a turn and successfully put a race in decline. Verify that tokens reduce to 1 per region, the banner grays out, and the power badge is removed. Verify Spirit and Ghoul exceptions work correctly. Implement a Playwright E2E test for the basic decline flow.

tasks.title: Add Race and Power Names as Text Labels in HUD
tasks.description: Display the names of races and powers as readable text labels in the combo shop HUD and player dashboards.
tasks.details: For each combo slot in the shop and in the active player dashboard area, add a text element (e.g., a `<span>` or a dedicated `Text` component) to display the `race.name` and `power.name`. Ensure these text labels are visually clear, legible at all zoom levels, and are present until artwork is introduced in Phase 3.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that race name and power name text labels appear in each of the 6 combo shop slots and in the active player dashboard area. Check for legibility and correct positioning.

tasks.title: Add Race and Power Ability Tooltips to HUD Combos
tasks.description: Provide hover tooltips for each race/power combo in the shop and for the player's active race banner and power badge, displaying their special ability descriptions.
tasks.details: Integrate a tooltip component with the combo shop slots and the player's active race banner/power badge. On hover, display the `race.abilityDescription` and `power.abilityDescription` from the game's data tables. Ensure these tooltips utilize the screen-space rendering fixed in task 39 for consistent sizing.
tasks.testStrategy: Hover over each combo in the shop and verify that a tooltip appears showing the correct race ability and power ability descriptions. Hover over the player's active race banner and power badge and verify tooltips appear with the correct text.

tasks.title: Add Player Box Ability Tooltips
tasks.description: Implement hover tooltips for the player info boxes (dashboard) to display the special abilities of the player's active race and power.
tasks.details: Similar to task 44, add hover tooltips to the player info boxes. When hovering over a player's active race banner or power badge within their dashboard, display the corresponding ability description. The tooltip content should match the descriptions used in the combo shop tooltips. Ensure this functionality works for all players' dashboards.
tasks.testStrategy: Hover over Player 1 and Player 2 info boxes. Verify that a tooltip appears showing the active race ability and power ability text for each player.

tasks.title: Highlight First-Conquest Eligible Regions Distinctly
tasks.description: Visually distinguish border and coastal regions as valid first conquest targets when a player has no regions owned.
tasks.details: When `getLegalActions()` (modified in task 41) identifies first-conquest eligible regions, apply a distinct visual highlight (e.g., a different color, a pulsating effect, or a unique border style) to these regions. This distinct highlight should only appear when the player begins their very first conquest (i.e., has no regions currently owned) and is in the conquest phase.
tasks.testStrategy: Start a new game and enter the conquest phase. Verify that border and coastal regions display the distinct first-conquest entry highlight, while inland regions are visually excluded from this special highlight.

tasks.title: Improve Reinforcement Die Visual Feedback
tasks.description: Display the result of the reinforcement die roll visually and clearly after it lands.
tasks.details: After the player rolls the reinforcement die, animate or display the result clearly showing which face value landed (0, 0, 0, 1, 2, or 3). This could be a temporary UI element showing the number, or an animation of a die model landing on the correct face. Ensure the result is visible before the conquest outcome resolves. Retain the existing tumble animation and wooden sound cue.
tasks.testStrategy: Roll the reinforcement die multiple times and verify that the landed value is displayed visually and clearly. Confirm that the result is shown before the conquest outcome is resolved.

tasks.title: Fix Reinforcement Die Flow Sequencing
tasks.description: Reorder the conquest phase UI to present the reinforcement die roll option before the 'End Conquest' button when a player has insufficient tokens for a standard conquest.
tasks.details: Adjust the UI logic in the conquest phase. When a player has at least 1 token remaining but cannot afford a standard conquest, the reinforcement die roll option should be presented as the primary action. The 'End Conquest' button should only appear after the player has either declined the die roll or after the die has been rolled.
tasks.testStrategy: Reach a point in the conquest phase where only 1 token remains. Verify that the die roll option appears before the 'End Conquest' button. Confirm that 'End Conquest' is still accessible if the player chooses not to roll or after the die has been rolled.

tasks.title: Allow Browsing Combo HUD During Any Turn Phase
tasks.description: Add a persistent button or control that allows players to open the combo shop HUD in a read-only browse mode at any time during their turn.
tasks.details: Implement a 'Browse Combos' button in the main game HUD. When clicked, open the Race & Power HUD in a special 'browse-only' state. In this mode, combo selection actions must be disabled, and the HUD should clearly indicate its read-only nature (e.g., with a 'Browse Mode' label). Closing the HUD should return the player to their current game phase without altering game state.
tasks.testStrategy: During a conquest phase, open the combo HUD in browse mode. Verify that combos are visible but clicking them does not trigger selection. Close the HUD and verify that the player returns to the correct game phase.

tasks.title: Implement Left/Right-Click Token Model for Redeployment
tasks.description: Enable left-click to add one token and right-click to remove one token from a region during the redeployment phase, enforcing a minimum of 1 token per occupied region.
tasks.details: Modify the redeployment phase interaction logic. Implement event listeners for left-click (add token) and right-click (remove token) on regions. Dynamically update token counts. Enforce a minimum of 1 token per occupied region throughout the process. The 'Confirm Redeployment' button must remain visible and accessible at all times during this phase.
tasks.testStrategy: In the redeployment phase, left-click to add tokens and right-click to remove tokens across multiple regions. Verify that the 1-token minimum per occupied region is enforced. Confirm that the 'Confirm Redeployment' button correctly completes the redeployment.

tasks.title: Add Interaction Mode / Pan Mode Toggle
tasks.description: Implement a toggle control (button or keyboard shortcut) to switch between 'Interaction mode' (default) and 'Pan mode' for map navigation.
tasks.details: Add a UI button (e.g., in the main HUD) or a keyboard shortcut (e.g., 'P') to toggle between modes. In 'Interaction mode', map clicks trigger game actions. In 'Pan mode', click-drag navigates the map without triggering any game actions; region hover highlights and tooltips should remain active, but clicks must not fire game actions. The current mode must be clearly indicated in the UI.
tasks.testStrategy: Toggle to Pan mode; click on a valid conquest target and verify no conquest action fires. Drag the map and verify panning works correctly. Toggle back to Interaction mode and verify that region clicks trigger game actions normally.

tasks.title: Redraw Region Polygons to Match Reference Map
tasks.description: Update the region hit polygons in `src/game/data/map2p.ts` to accurately reflect the boundaries shown in the background map image.
tasks.details: Manually retrace and update all region polygon vertex arrays in `src/game/data/map2p.ts` to precisely match the visual boundaries in `src/assets/reference/2-player-map.jpeg`. Verify and update adjacency relationships and region center points if necessary to maintain game logic integrity after the redraw.
tasks.testStrategy: Click along the visual borders of various regions and verify that the hit zones accurately match what is shown in the map image. Confirm that all adjacency relationships remain correct after the update.

tasks.title: Phase 2 Full Regression Testing
tasks.description: Conduct a full regression test suite to verify all Phase 1 functionality remains intact and all Phase 2 features work correctly.
tasks.details: Write new Playwright E2E tests covering: decline flow, first conquest entry restriction, conquest cost display, die roll sequencing, redeployment left/right-click model, interaction/pan mode toggle, HUD browse mode, and player box tooltips. Execute the complete E2E test suite (all Phase 1 E2E tests plus new Phase 2 tests) across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. Ensure all unit tests also pass. Fix any regressions found.
tasks.testStrategy: Achieve 0 failures across the full Playwright E2E test suite running on Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. Ensure all unit tests pass without errors.

tasks.title: Define Game State Types and Interfaces
tasks.description: Create all TypeScript interfaces for the immutable game state model: GameState, PlayerState, ActiveRaceState, DeclinedRaceState, BoardState, RegionState, ComboShopState, ComboSlot, and all union/enum types (TurnPhase, Terrain, RaceId, PowerId). Also define the GameAction union type and GameLogEntry. All state types must be readonly/immutable. Place in src/game/state/types.ts. ActiveRaceState must include maxSupply to track the finite token limit per race. Each race has a maximum token supply (e.g., Amazons 15, Skeletons 20) that caps token-generating abilities.
tasks.details: Reference design/technical-design.md section 2 for the full type definitions. This is the foundational layer — all other tasks depend on these types being correct and complete. Note: each race has a finite maxSupply of tokens (see PRD race table). ActiveRaceState needs a maxSupply field. Lost Tribes have a supply of 18.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: verify types compile with strict TypeScript, create sample state objects to confirm structure.

tasks.title: Author 2-Player Map Data (Polygons, Adjacency, Properties)
tasks.description: Hand-trace polygon coordinates for all regions on the 2-player map from src/assets/reference/2-player-map.jpeg. Create src/game/data/map2p.ts exporting a MapData object with: region polygons (vertex arrays relative to map image), center points, adjacency lists, terrain types, edge/coastal flags, and initial markers (lost tribes, mountains, mines, magic sources, caverns). Coordinates are in pixels relative to map image top-left.
tasks.details: The 2-player map has approximately 16 regions. Each region needs: id, name, terrain, polygon vertices (clockwise), center point, adjacentRegionIds, isEdge, isCoastal, hasMountain, hasMine, hasMagicSource, hasCavern, hasLostTribe. Adjacency must be symmetric. Reference the rulebook and map image.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: verify adjacency symmetry, all regions have required fields, polygon vertices are valid, edge regions actually border the map edge.

tasks.title: Define Race and Power Data Tables
tasks.description: Create src/game/data/races.ts with RaceDefinition records for all 14 races (token counts, max supply, modifier tags, tooltips) and src/game/data/powers.ts with PowerDefinition records for all 20 powers (bonus token counts, modifier tags, tooltips). Use the AbilityModifiers interface from the modifier/tag system design. Each race must include maxSupply field.
tasks.details: Each race/power has declarative modifiers where possible (conquestCostModifier, bonusPerTerrain, etc.) and a customHandler key for complex abilities (Sorcerers, Dragon Master, Halflings, Diplomat, Heroic). Reference PRD race/power tables and design/technical-design.md section 4. Max supply per race: Amazons 15, Dwarves 8, Elves 11, Ghouls 10, Giants 11, Halflings 11, Humans 10, Orcs 10, Ratmen 13, Skeletons 20, Sorcerers 18, Tritons 11, Trolls 10, Wizards 10. Lost Tribes: 18. Token-generating abilities (Skeletons, Sorcerers) are capped by maxSupply.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: verify all 14 races and 20 powers are defined, token counts match PRD, modifier types are valid.

tasks.title: Implement Ability Modifier System
tasks.description: Create src/game/abilities/modifiers.ts with the AbilityModifiers interface and a getActiveModifiers() function that merges race + power modifiers for the active player. Create src/game/abilities/raceAbilities.ts and powerAbilities.ts with CustomAbilityHandler registrations for complex abilities (Sorcerers, Dragon Master, Halflings, Diplomat, Heroic, Bivouacking, Fortified, Amazons).
tasks.details: The modifier system is the core of the ability architecture. ~70% of abilities are pure data (modifier tags), ~30% need custom handler functions with hooks: modifyLegalActions, onConquest, onDecline, onTurnEnd, onTurnStart. Reference design/technical-design.md section 4.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test modifier merging for several race/power combos, verify custom handlers are invoked at correct lifecycle points.

tasks.title: Implement Game Setup and Initial State Creation
tasks.description: Create src/game/engine/setup.ts with createInitialState() that produces a valid starting GameState: randomly select first player, shuffle race and power decks, deal 6 combos to shop, place lost tribes and mountain tokens on the board per map data, set turn to 1, give each player 5 coins, set phase to 'selectCombo'.
tasks.details: Must use the map data from map2p.ts for initial region state (lost tribes, mountains). Race/power decks are shuffled randomly. The state returned must be fully immutable.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: verify initial state has correct turn/phase/coins, 6 combos in shop, lost tribes placed on correct regions, mountain tokens placed.

tasks.title: Implement Combo Shop Logic
tasks.description: Create src/game/engine/comboShop.ts with: selectCombo(state, comboIndex) — applies coin cost for skipping, awards combo's coins to player, sets player's active race with correct token count (race base + power bonus), and replenishes the shop by shifting combos up and dealing a new one from the decks.
tasks.details: Top combo (index 0) is free. Each lower position costs 1 coin per skipped slot. Coins placed on skipped combos stay on those combos. When selected, player gets any coins sitting on the combo. Shop replenishes by shifting up and revealing new combo at bottom. Reference PRD FR-8 through FR-12.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test free selection, paid selection with coin placement, coin collection from combo, shop replenishment, deck exhaustion edge case.

tasks.title: Implement Conquest Cost Calculation
tasks.description: Create src/game/engine/conquestCost.ts with calculateConquestCost(state, regionId) that computes tokens needed: 2 base + region contents (tokens, lost tribe, mountain, troll lair, fortress, encampment) + ability modifiers (Commando, Mounted, Tritons, Giants, Underworld, Dragon Master). Minimum cost is 1.
tasks.details: Must apply all conquest cost modifiers from the active race/power combo. Giants get -1 for regions adjacent to their own mountain regions. Underworld gets -1 on cavern regions. Commando gets -1 on all regions. Mounted gets -1 on hill/farmland. Tritons get -1 on coastal. Reference PRD FR-15.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test base cost, cost with each modifier type, stacking modifiers, minimum cost of 1, all terrain/defense combinations.

tasks.title: Implement Legal Action Generation
tasks.description: Create src/game/engine/legalActions.ts with getLegalActions(state) that returns all valid GameActions for the current phase and active player. Must handle: selectCombo (which combos are affordable), readyTroops (which regions can have tokens picked up), conquest (valid targets based on adjacency/edge/abilities), reinforcementDie (eligible target), redeploy (valid distributions), decline (when allowed).
tasks.details: First conquest must target edge/coastal region (unless Halflings/Flying). Subsequent conquests must be adjacent to owned regions (unless Flying/Underworld cavern adjacency). Seas/Lakes not conquerable unless Seafaring. Must include ability-specific actions (Sorcerer convert, Dragon placement, etc.). Reference PRD FR-13 through FR-18.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test legal actions per phase, first conquest restrictions, adjacency rules, Flying override, Seafaring seas, Halfling anywhere entry.

tasks.title: Implement Phase State Machine
tasks.description: Create src/game/engine/phaseTransition.ts with getNextPhase(state, completedAction) implementing the turn phase state machine: selectCombo → readyTroops → conquest → reinforcementDie → redeploy → score → (optional decline for Stout). Handle conditional transitions: skip selectCombo if player has active race, skip reinforcementDie if not eligible, Ghoul decline conquest before active race.
tasks.details: Phase transitions must account for: Stout power (decline after scoring), Ghouls in decline (conquest before active race), decline replacing the conquest sequence, turn advancement and player switching, game over detection at turn 10. Reference design/technical-design.md section 3.3.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test full turn flow, conditional phase skipping, Stout decline path, Ghoul pre-conquest, decline turn flow, game over transition.

tasks.title: Implement Core Action Application (applyAction)
tasks.description: Create src/game/engine/actions.ts with applyAction(state, action) that validates the action is legal, applies it to produce a new immutable GameState, appends to the action log, and transitions the phase. This is the central state transition function that delegates to specific handlers (comboShop, conquest, decline, redeployment, etc.).
tasks.details: Must handle all GameAction types. Conquest actions must: place attacker tokens, handle defeated tokens (1 discarded, rest returned to defender), handle Lost Tribe/single In Decline token removal, update region ownership. Must enforce immutability — never mutate input state. Reference PRD FR-13 through FR-28.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test each action type produces correct new state, original state unchanged, illegal actions rejected, action log appended.

tasks.title: Implement Decline Mechanics
tasks.description: Create src/game/engine/decline.ts with applyDecline(state) handling: remove previous declined race (unless Spirit), flip active race to declined, reduce to 1 token per region (unless Ghouls), remove power badge (unless Spirit), clear special markers. Handle Spirit exception (declined race survives alongside new decline) and Stout exception (decline after conquest turn).
tasks.details: Decline edge cases: Spirit-powered race tokens stay when player declines again. Ghouls keep all tokens (don't reduce to 1). Stout allows decline at end of regular turn. Max 2 declined races (1 Spirit + 1 other). Troll lairs and fortresses persist in decline. Reference PRD FR-22 through FR-25a.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test basic decline, Spirit exception, Ghoul full-token decline, Stout end-of-turn decline, previous decline removal, special marker persistence.

tasks.title: Implement Scoring Engine
tasks.description: Create src/game/engine/scoring.ts with calculateScore(state, playerIndex) that computes end-of-turn victory coins: 1 per occupied region (active + declined) + all race/power bonuses (terrain bonuses, Merchant, Alchemist, Wealthy first-turn, Orcs/Pillaging per conquest, Dwarves mines in decline).
tasks.details: Must correctly apply: base 1 coin per region, Humans (+1 farmland), Wizards (+1 magic), Forest/Hill/Swamp power terrain bonuses, Dwarves (+1 mine, active and decline), Merchant (+1 per region), Alchemist (+2 flat), Wealthy (+7 first turn only), Orcs/Pillaging (+1 per non-empty conquered region this turn), Fortified (+1 per fortress, active only). Reference PRD FR-29 through FR-32.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test base scoring, each race bonus, each power bonus, combined race+power scoring, decline region scoring, Wealthy first-turn-only.

tasks.title: Implement Reinforcement Die
tasks.description: Create src/game/engine/reinforcementDie.ts with rollDie() returning a random result from [0,0,0,1,2,3] and resolveReinforcement(state, regionId, dieResult) that attempts final conquest with available tokens + die result. On success, place tokens. On failure, tokens return to player's regions via redeployment. Die ends conquest phase regardless.
tasks.details: Die available when player has at least 1 token but not enough for standard conquest. Die sides: 0,0,0,1,2,3. Success = available tokens + die result >= conquest cost. Failure = tokens placed back in previously occupied regions. No further conquests after die regardless of result. Reference PRD FR-19 through FR-21a.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test die roll distribution, successful reinforcement conquest, failed reinforcement, tokens returned on failure, phase ends after die.

tasks.title: Implement Ready Troops Phase
tasks.description: Implement the readyTroops phase logic: player may pick up Active tokens from occupied regions (leaving at least 1 per region to keep control), or abandon regions entirely by picking up all tokens. Picked-up tokens are added to available hand for conquest. Integrate with legalActions and applyAction.
tasks.details: Player picks up tokens before conquering to reuse them offensively. Must leave at least 1 token in regions they want to keep. Can abandon entirely (pick up all, lose control). Reference PRD FR-13a through FR-13c.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test picking up tokens, minimum 1 left requirement, full region abandonment, tokens added to hand correctly.

tasks.title: Implement Redeployment Phase
tasks.description: Implement src/game/engine/redeployment.ts with applyRedeployment(state, deployment) that redistributes active tokens among occupied regions. Enforce minimum 1 token per occupied region. Also handle defender redeployment (defeated tokens placed in other owned regions at end of attacker's turn).
tasks.details: Deployment is a map of regionId → tokenCount. Sum of all tokens must equal player's total active tokens. Each occupied region must have at least 1. Defender redeployment happens at end of active player's turn. If defender has no regions, they deploy on their next turn as first conquest. Reference PRD FR-26 through FR-28, FR-18b.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test valid redeployment, minimum token enforcement, defender redeployment, no-region defender case.

tasks.title: Set Up Board Scene with Map Image and Hit Polygons
tasks.description: Create src/game/scenes/Board.ts Phaser scene with: pre-rendered map image as background, invisible interactive polygon hit zones for each region (from map2p.ts data), Phaser camera pan/zoom (pointer drag + scroll wheel), min/max zoom bounds. Regions emit click/hover events.
tasks.details: Use Phaser's built-in camera system for pan/zoom. Hit zones are Phaser.GameObjects.Polygon with setInteractive(). Map image loaded in Boot scene. Camera bounds set to map image dimensions with some padding. Region hover should show a subtle highlight. Reference design/technical-design.md sections 5.2 and 8.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright: verify map renders, regions are clickable, pan/zoom works, camera stays within bounds.

tasks.title: Set Up HUD Scene with Turn Track and Player Dashboards
tasks.description: Create src/game/scenes/HUD.ts Phaser scene running in parallel with Board scene. Fixed camera (no pan/zoom). Display: turn track (1-10), current phase indicator, active player highlight, player dashboards (race banner, power badge, token count, victory coins), and context-sensitive action buttons (End Conquest, Decline, Roll Die, Confirm Redeploy).
tasks.details: HUD scene listens to GameController events to update display. Action buttons emit playerAction events for HumanPlayer. Use Phaser text/graphics for placeholder rendering. Layout: turn track top-left, phase indicator top-center, dashboards bottom-left/right, action panel bottom-center. Reference design/technical-design.md section 5.3.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright: verify HUD renders over board, turn track visible, dashboards show player info, action buttons respond to clicks.

tasks.title: Implement Placeholder Token Renderer
tasks.description: Create src/game/presentation/TokenRenderer.ts with PlaceholderTokenRenderer that draws colored circles with race initial letters for tokens on the board. Player 1 gets blue tones, Player 2 gets red tones. Active tokens are solid with bold borders, declined tokens are gray with dashed borders and reduced alpha. Tokens cluster around region centers.
tasks.details: Token stacking: 1 token centered, 2-3 triangular, 4+ circular with count label. Must support special markers (Troll lair, fortress, encampment, Hole-in-the-Ground, hero, dragon) as distinct shapes or icons. Reference design/technical-design.md section 10.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright: verify tokens render in correct regions, player colors are distinct, declined tokens visually different from active.

tasks.title: Implement Region Overlay Renderer
tasks.description: Create src/game/presentation/RegionRenderer.ts that draws vector overlays on top of the map image: ownership borders (player-colored, solid for active, dashed for declined), valid target highlights (pulsing glow), selection highlight, and special region markers. Listens to state changes to update overlays.
tasks.details: Overlays use Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics drawn on top of the map image layer but below the token layer. Active regions have bold colored borders matching player color. Declined regions have faded/dashed borders. Valid conquest targets pulse/glow when in conquest phase. Reference PRD visual design principles.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright: verify region borders appear with correct colors, valid targets highlight during conquest phase.

tasks.title: Implement GameController and Game Loop
tasks.description: Create src/game/GameController.ts that orchestrates the game loop: create initial state, alternate between players, get legal actions, wait for player decision (via IPlayer), compute new state via applyAction, trigger animations via choreographer, commit state, emit events for scene updates. Connect Board and HUD scenes to the controller via event bus.
tasks.details: The game loop is async: state → render → wait for player → animate → commit. Use Phaser.Events.EventEmitter as the shared event bus. GameController holds the canonical game state. Scenes are purely reactive (read state, render, emit user input). Reference design/technical-design.md section 5.4.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test game loop with mock IPlayers, verify state progression through full turn cycle. Playwright: test full turn in browser.

tasks.title: Implement IPlayer Interface and HumanPlayer
tasks.description: Create src/game/players/IPlayer.ts with the async IPlayer interface, and src/game/players/HumanPlayer.ts that resolves chooseAction when the user clicks a valid UI element. HumanPlayer listens to 'playerAction' events from the Board/HUD scenes and resolves the pending promise.
tasks.details: IPlayer.chooseAction(state, legalActions) returns Promise<GameAction>. HumanPlayer creates a promise that resolves when eventBus emits 'playerAction'. Must handle phase-specific input: clicking regions for conquest, clicking combos for selection, clicking deploy button, etc. Reference design/technical-design.md section 8.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test HumanPlayer resolves on event emission. Playwright: test clicking a valid target resolves the action.

tasks.title: Implement Animation Choreographer
tasks.description: Create src/game/presentation/AnimationChoreographer.ts that translates GameActions into Phaser tween sequences. Implement animations for: conquest (tokens slide in, defenders scatter), combo selection (coins animate, tokens appear), decline (banners flip gray, tokens reduce), redeployment (tokens slide between regions), reinforcement die (tumble animation), scoring (coin cascade).
tasks.details: Each animation is an async method returning a Promise that resolves when the tween sequence completes. Supports speed multiplier for AI-vs-AI playback. Camera auto-focuses on relevant area before each animation. Reference design/technical-design.md section 6.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright: verify animations play without errors, tokens end up in correct positions after animation.

tasks.title: Implement Stubbed Audio Manager
tasks.description: Create src/game/presentation/AudioManager.ts with the IAudioManager interface and StubAudioManager implementation. All methods are no-ops that optionally log to console in dev mode. Wire into AnimationChoreographer so audio calls are made at correct moments but produce no sound.
tasks.details: Interface methods: playTokenPlace, playTokenSlide, playConquest, playDieRoll, playCoinScore, playDecline, playTurnTransition, playVictory, setAmbient, setVolume. Will be replaced with PhaserAudioManager in M5. Reference design/technical-design.md section 7.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: verify stub methods exist and don't throw.

tasks.title: Implement Combo Shop UI
tasks.description: Add combo shop display to the Board or HUD scene: 6 visible race/power combos in a vertical column, coin indicators on skipped combos, clickable selection. Show race name, power name, token count, and cost. Coins animate from player to skipped combos on selection. Shop replenishes visually after selection.
tasks.details: Shop is displayed spatially on the canvas (right of map) or as a panel in HUD. Each combo shows race banner + power badge (placeholder text/icons for now). Top combo marked as 'FREE', others show coin cost. Player's available coins displayed. Reference PRD FR-8 through FR-12, interaction flow step 1.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright: verify 6 combos display, clicking a combo triggers selection, coins animate correctly, shop replenishes.

tasks.title: Implement Easy AI Player
tasks.description: Create src/game/players/AIPlayer.ts with easy difficulty: makes random but valid choices from getLegalActions(). Add configurable delay between actions for visual pacing. Implement for all action types: combo selection, conquest target, redeployment, decline decision.
tasks.details: Easy AI picks randomly from legal actions with slight bias toward undefended regions for conquest. Decline decision is random (10% chance per turn). Redeployment distributes tokens evenly. Must work with the IPlayer async interface. Reference design/technical-design.md section 8.2 and AI opponent design doc.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test AI always returns legal actions, full game simulation completes without errors (random vs random).

tasks.title: Implement Medium AI Player
tasks.description: Extend AIPlayer with medium difficulty: heuristic evaluation for all decisions. Combo selection scores synergy with board state. Conquest prioritizes high-value low-cost targets. Decline considers remaining productivity vs best available combo. Redeployment defends borders.
tasks.details: Heuristic evaluators: ComboRanker (score combo by token count, terrain synergy, opponent vulnerability), ConquestPlanner (greedy: maximize coins gained per token spent), DeclineOracle (compare current race productivity to best combo value), TokenDeployer (stack borders adjacent to opponent). Reference AI opponent design doc section 3.
tasks.testStrategy: Vitest: test heuristic evaluators produce reasonable rankings, medium AI beats easy AI >60% of the time over 100 simulated games.

tasks.title: Implement End Game Screen
tasks.description: Create end-game UI displayed when phase reaches 'gameOver': final scores for both players, winner announcement, score breakdown by turn (from game log), tiebreaker display if needed (most race tokens on board). Offer 'New Game' and 'Main Menu' buttons.
tasks.details: Tiebreaker: if coin totals are equal, player with most race tokens (Active + In Decline) on the board wins. Score breakdown uses the GameLogEntry history to show coins earned per turn. Victory fanfare animation (placeholder for now). Reference PRD FR-39 through FR-42.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright: verify end screen shows after turn 10, correct winner displayed, new game button works.

tasks.title: Implement Contextual Tooltips
tasks.description: Add hover tooltips to all interactive game elements: regions (terrain type, defense value, owner), race banners (race ability description), power badges (power ability description), combo shop entries (full details), tokens (race name, active/declined). Use Phaser text objects positioned near the hovered element.
tasks.details: Tooltips appear on pointer hover with a small delay (~300ms). Positioned to avoid going off-screen. Include race/power ability descriptions from the data tables. Valid action hints during conquest phase ('Click to conquer — costs 3 tokens'). Reference PRD US-12, FR-33, FR-35.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright: verify tooltip appears on hover over region, shows correct terrain info, tooltip for race shows ability text.

tasks.title: Set Up Vitest for Unit Testing
tasks.description: Install and configure Vitest for the project. Create vitest.config.ts with TypeScript support, path aliases matching vite.config.ts (@/ → src/), and coverage reporting. Create test directory structure under tests/unit/. Write a sample test to verify setup works.
tasks.details: Vitest integrates natively with Vite. Configure to use the same tsconfig and path aliases. Set up coverage with v8 or istanbul provider. Tests use .test.ts extension. Run with 'npx vitest' or add npm script.
tasks.testStrategy: Run vitest and verify sample test passes.

tasks.title: Implement Main Menu with Game Mode Selection
tasks.description: Update src/game/scenes/MainMenu.ts to offer game mode selection: Human vs Human, Human vs AI (with difficulty selector: Easy/Medium), and AI vs AI (with speed control). Selected mode configures which IPlayer implementations are used. Transition to Board + HUD scenes with the configured GameController.
tasks.details: Main menu should display: game title, mode selection buttons, difficulty dropdown for AI modes, 'Start Game' button. AI vs AI mode includes playback speed control (0.5x, 1x, 2x, 4x). Reference PRD play modes: Human vs Human (hot-seat), Human vs AI, AI vs AI.
tasks.testStrategy: Playwright: verify menu renders, mode selection works, game starts with correct player types.

tasks.title: Run Main Menu e2e tests
tasks.description: Execute the Playwright e2e test suite for the main menu: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/mainMenu.spec.ts --reporter=line`. Verify all 8 tests pass across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. Tests cover: page load, canvas render, correct page title, MainMenu scene activation, HvH default mode, HvAI mode selection, medium difficulty selection, scene launch, and browser refresh.
tasks.details:
Command: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/mainMenu.spec.ts --reporter=line`
Expected: 8 tests × 3 browsers = 24 test runs, all passing.
Test file: tests/e2e/mainMenu.spec.ts
Results saved to: playwright-report/index.html
tasks.testStrategy: Mark done when all 8 tests pass on all 3 browsers with 0 failures.

tasks.title: Run Human vs Human e2e tests
tasks.description: Execute the Playwright e2e test suite for HvH game flow: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/hvhGame.spec.ts --reporter=line`. Verify all 14 tests pass. Tests cover: initial game state, combo selection, phase progression (readyTroops → conquest → reinforcementDie → redeploy → score), full turn completion, turn advance, player switching, and state immutability.
tasks.details:
Command: `npx playwright test tests/e2e/hvhGame.spec.ts --reporter=line`
Expected: 14 tests × 3 browsers = 42 test runs, all passing.
Test file: tests/e2e/hvhGame.spec.ts
Note: Tests require the dev server running (handled automatically by playwright.config.ts webServer).
tasks.testStrategy: Mark done when all 14 tests pass on all 3 browsers with 0 failures.

tasks.title: Run Human vs AI e2e tests

Tests cover: HvAI Easy and Medium game start, human player interaction, AI auto-turn completion (both difficulties), turn advance, multi-turn flow, coin accumulation, and zero JS errors.
tasks.details:

Expected: 12 tests × 3 browsers = 36 test runs, all passing.

tasks.title: Run full e2e test suite and review results
tasks.description: Execute the complete Playwright e2e suite across all test files: `npx playwright test --reporter=html`. Open the HTML report (`npx playwright show-report`) and review all results. Confirm 0 failures across all browsers. Screenshot/trace artifacts for any failures should be reviewed in the report.
tasks.details:

Expected: All e2e tests pass (mainMenu + hvhGame + hvaiGame) across Chromium, Firefox, WebKit.
Artifacts: playwright-report/index.html contains traces for any failures.
Note: This is the gate check before considering e2e coverage complete.

tasks.title: Fix any failing e2e tests
tasks.description: Investigate and fix any test failures found in task 34. Common failure modes: timing issues (increase timeouts or add waitForFunction), coordinate mismatches (verify game pixel coordinates against current scene layout), canvas scaling issues (verify clickGame helper scales correctly), Phaser scene lifecycle races (add waitForScene before state checks).
tasks.details:
Debugging steps:
1. Run `npx playwright test --debug` to step through failing tests interactively
2. Run `npx playwright test --headed` to watch the browser during test execution
3. Use `npx playwright show-report` to view traces and screenshots of failures
4. Check console logs with `page.on('console', ...)` for Phaser errors
5. Verify __phaserGame is exposed correctly in tests/e2e/helpers.ts
tasks.testStrategy: Mark done when task 34 can be re-run with 0 failures.

tasks.title: Fix Map Image Viewport Clipping
tasks.description: The map image is clipped at the bottom of the screen, cutting off the round 8, 9, and 10 markers on the turn track. Fix the viewport/container sizing in the Board scene so the entire map image is accessible when panning and zooming.
tasks.details: Investigate the Board scene camera bounds, container sizing, and Phaser world bounds configuration. The full map including all turn markers must be reachable. Likely fix involves adjusting camera.setBounds() or the map image container dimensions.
tasks.testStrategy: Visually verify the bottom of the map including turn 8, 9, 10 markers is reachable by panning/zooming. Add Playwright E2E assertion that the map image height is fully rendered.

tasks.title: Fix Race & Power HUD Interaction Passthrough (FR-55)
tasks.description: When the Race & Power selection HUD is open, map region tooltips and click handlers activate behind it. Fix the HUD to fully capture pointer events and block all map interaction while it is open. References: FR-55.
tasks.details: While the Race & Power HUD is visible, disable all Board scene region pointer events (hover, click) and suppress any active tooltips. The HUD must set a flag or emit an event that the Board scene and tooltip system respect. On HUD close, re-enable map interactions.
tasks.testStrategy: Open the Race & Power HUD, hover over HUD options, verify no map tooltips appear and no region clicks fire. Playwright E2E test to confirm no tooltip DOM elements appear behind the HUD.

tasks.title: Fix Initial Camera Zoom Level (FR-58)
tasks.description: The Board scene camera starts zoomed in rather than at maximum zoom-out. Set the initial zoom so the entire map fits on screen when the game starts. Region hit polygon scaling must remain accurate at the new default zoom. References: FR-58.
tasks.details: Calculate the correct initial zoom level by dividing the canvas height/width by the map image height/width and taking the minimum. Set camera zoom to this value in Board.create(). Verify that Phaser.GameObjects.Polygon hit zones scale correctly with the camera zoom.
tasks.testStrategy: Start a new game and verify the entire map is visible without any panning or zoom adjustment. Verify region hit zones register clicks accurately at default zoom. Playwright E2E screenshot comparison.

tasks.title: Fix Tooltip Zoom Scaling (FR-59)
tasks.description: Tooltips currently scale with the camera zoom, appearing huge when zoomed in and tiny when zoomed out. Refactor tooltip rendering to use screen-space coordinates so font size and panel dimensions remain constant at all zoom levels. References: FR-59.
tasks.details: Tooltips must be rendered in the HUD scene (fixed camera) or positioned using camera.getWorldPoint() to translate to screen coordinates. Move tooltip GameObjects to the HUD scene if they are currently in the Board scene, or use setScrollFactor(0) and manually position relative to the pointer in screen space.
tasks.testStrategy: Hover over a region at minimum zoom, maximum zoom, and mid zoom — verify the tooltip appears identical in size and readability at all levels.

tasks.title: Fix Decline Flow — Surface Decline Option to Player (FR-22)
tasks.description: The Decline button is not presented to the player during their turn, making the decline mechanic inaccessible from the UI. Wire up the Decline action so it appears at the correct phase and invokes the existing applyDecline() engine function. References: FR-22, FR-23, FR-23a, FR-24, FR-25, FR-25a.
tasks.details: The Decline button should be available in the HUD during the conquest phase (as an alternative to conquering) and after scoring for players with Stout power. It must be hidden during phases where decline is not legal (e.g., first turn before selecting a combo, or if already declined this turn). On click, dispatch the decline GameAction through the GameController. The full decline animation must play: banner flip to gray, token reduction to 1 per region (except Ghouls), power badge removal (except Spirit).
tasks.testStrategy: Play through a turn and click Decline. Verify tokens reduce to 1 per region, banner grays out, power badge is removed. Test Ghoul exception (all tokens stay). Test Spirit exception (badge stays). Playwright E2E test for the basic decline flow.

tasks.title: Fix First Conquest Entry Rule Enforcement (FR-13)
tasks.description: The game allows the first conquest to target any region, violating the rule that the first conquest must target a border (map edge) or coastal (Sea/Lake-adjacent) region. Fix getLegalActions() to enforce this restriction, with correct exceptions for Halflings and Flying. References: FR-13.
tasks.details: In getLegalActions(), when the active player has no currently occupied regions (tokensInHand > 0, no owned regions), filter conquest targets to only isEdge or isCoastal regions. Check for Halflings race and Flying power modifiers which override this restriction and allow any region. Verify that subsequent conquests (after the first region is taken) correctly use adjacency rules instead.
tasks.testStrategy: Start a game, enter conquest phase with no regions owned. Verify only border/coastal regions are highlighted as valid targets. Attempt to click a non-border non-coastal region and verify nothing happens. Start again as Halflings and verify all regions are valid. Playwright E2E test.

tasks.title: Fix Conquest Cost Calculation and Tooltip Display (FR-15)
tasks.description: The conquest cost tooltip shows a flat 2 regardless of defenders. Fix calculateConquestCost() to correctly compute 2 (base) + 1 per Mountain + 1 per Encampment + 1 per Fortress + 1 per Troll's Lair + 1 per Lost Tribe token + 1 per enemy race token. Update the tooltip to display the correct cost. References: FR-15.
tasks.details: Review calculateConquestCost() in src/game/engine/conquestCost.ts. Ensure it reads region state correctly: mountain tokens, special markers (encampment, fortress, troll lair), lost tribe presence, and enemy token count. The conquest tooltip must call calculateConquestCost() and display the result. Also verify the game rejects conquest attempts where the player has fewer tokens than the cost.
tasks.testStrategy: Hover over a region with a mountain token — tooltip should show cost 3. Hover over a region with 2 enemy tokens — tooltip should show cost 4. Hover over a region with a Lost Tribe — tooltip should show cost 3. Attempt to conquer a region with insufficient tokens and verify it is rejected.

tasks.title: Add Race and Power Names as Text Labels in HUD (FR-53)
tasks.description: The combo shop HUD and player dashboards do not display race and power names as readable text, making combos unidentifiable without artwork. Add text labels for race name and power name to each combo slot in the shop and to the active player dashboard. References: FR-53.
tasks.details: Update the combo shop UI rendering to display the race name and power name as Phaser Text objects within each combo slot. Also update the player dashboard to show the active race name and power name as text. Use the name fields from the RaceDefinition and PowerDefinition data tables. Text must be legible at default zoom.
tasks.testStrategy: Start a game and verify all 6 combo shop slots show a race name and power name. Verify the active player dashboard shows the selected race name and power name after combo selection.

tasks.title: Add Race and Power Ability Tooltips to HUD Combos (FR-33, FR-35)
tasks.description: The combo shop and player dashboards do not show race and power special ability descriptions. Add hover tooltips to each combo in the shop and to the player's active race banner and power badge. References: FR-33, FR-35.
tasks.details: Use the tooltip descriptions already defined in the RaceDefinition and PowerDefinition data tables. On hover over a combo slot, show the race ability and power ability text in a tooltip panel. On hover over the player's active race banner, show the race ability. On hover over the power badge, show the power ability. Reuse the existing tooltip system.
tasks.testStrategy: Hover over each of the 6 combo shop slots and verify a tooltip appears with the race ability and power ability text. Hover over the active player race banner and power badge and verify correct tooltips appear.

tasks.title: Allow Browsing Combo HUD During Any Turn Phase (FR-54)
tasks.description: Players can only see the Race & Power combo shop during the selection phase. Add a persistent control that opens the HUD in a read-only browse mode during any phase so players can preview upcoming combos. References: FR-54.
tasks.details: Add a button to the HUD (e.g., near the combo shop area) labeled 'View Shop' or similar that is always visible during a player's turn. When clicked during a non-selection phase, it opens the combo HUD in browse-only mode: combos are displayed with names and tooltips but clicking them does not trigger selection. The HUD must display a clear visual indicator that it is in browse mode (e.g., greyed-out combo slots, 'Browse Only' label). Closing the HUD returns to the current phase without state change.
tasks.testStrategy: During conquest phase, click the browse button. Verify the combo shop opens showing all combos. Click a combo and verify no selection action fires. Close the HUD and verify conquest phase continues normally.

tasks.title: Highlight First-Conquest Eligible Regions Distinctly (FR-56)
tasks.description: Border and coastal regions eligible for the player's first conquest are not visually distinguished from other regions. Apply a distinct highlight to these entry regions when the player has no owned regions, separate from the standard valid-target highlight used for subsequent conquests. References: FR-56.
tasks.details: In RegionRenderer, detect when the player is about to make their first conquest (no currently owned regions). In this state, render border/coastal valid targets with a distinct visual treatment — for example, a pulsing gold or white border — while non-eligible regions remain visually muted or show a different style. This is in addition to the existing conquest-phase highlighting. Remove the distinct highlight after the first conquest is made.
tasks.testStrategy: Start a new game and enter conquest phase. Verify border/coastal regions show the distinct first-conquest entry highlight. Verify inland regions do not show this highlight. After conquering the first region, verify the highlight reverts to standard conquest highlighting.

tasks.title: Improve Reinforcement Die Visual Feedback (FR-20, FR-21)
tasks.description: After rolling the reinforcement die, the result is not shown visually. Display the landed die face value clearly before the conquest outcome resolves. References: FR-20, FR-21.
tasks.details: After rollDie() returns a result, animate or display the die face result in the UI (e.g., a large number or die face icon in the die area of the HUD). The display must appear before the conquest resolution plays out. Keep the existing tumble animation. The result display should remain visible for at least 1.5 seconds so the player can read it before the conquest animation begins.
tasks.testStrategy: Roll the reinforcement die and verify the result value (0, 1, 2, or 3) is displayed visibly in the UI before the conquest resolves. Verify the display appears for enough time to be readable.

tasks.title: Fix Reinforcement Die Flow Sequencing (FR-19)
tasks.description: The End Conquest button currently appears before the reinforcement die option when the player has 1 token remaining. Reorder the UI so the die roll is the primary action when the player has at least 1 token but cannot afford a standard conquest. References: FR-19.
tasks.details: In the HUD conquest action panel, when getLegalActions() returns a reinforcementDie action as available, display the Roll Die button as the primary/prominent action. The End Conquest button should be secondary or only appear after the player explicitly dismisses the die option. After the die is rolled (regardless of result), End Conquest becomes the only option. Reference PRD FR-19 and FR-21a.
tasks.testStrategy: Reach the state where only 1 token is in hand. Verify Roll Die button is displayed before End Conquest. Roll the die and verify End Conquest is the only option afterward. Verify End Conquest is still reachable if the player chooses not to roll.

tasks.title: Implement Left/Right-Click Token Model for Redeployment (FR-57)
tasks.description: The redeployment phase lacks precise token control. Implement left-click to add one token and right-click to remove one token from a region during redeployment. Players must be able to freely adjust token distribution until confirming. References: FR-57, FR-26, FR-27.
tasks.details: In the Board scene, during the redeployment phase, register both left-click (pointer down, button 0) and right-click (pointer down, button 2) on region hit zones. Left-click moves one token from the player's undeployed hand to the clicked region (if the player has tokens to place). Right-click moves one token from the clicked region back to the player's hand (only if the region has more than 1 token — enforce the minimum 1 per occupied region). Update the region overlay and token display reactively. The Confirm Redeployment button must always be visible. Prevent browser context menu on right-click.
tasks.testStrategy: In redeployment phase, left-click a region to add a token. Right-click a region to remove a token. Verify the 1-token minimum prevents right-clicking below 1. Confirm redeployment and verify state is correct. Test that right-click does not open the browser context menu.

tasks.title: Add Interaction Mode / Pan Mode Toggle (FR-60, US-15)
tasks.description: Players have no way to navigate the map without risking accidental game actions. Add a toggle between Interaction mode (clicks trigger game actions) and Pan mode (click-drag navigates without triggering actions). References: FR-60, US-15.
tasks.details: Add a toggle button in the HUD (e.g., a cursor/hand icon toggle). Default mode is Interaction. In Pan mode: disable all region click handlers on the Board scene; pointer drag pans the camera as normal; region hover highlights and tooltips remain active but do not trigger actions. In Interaction mode: restore all region click handlers. The current mode must be clearly indicated by the button state. Optionally support a keyboard shortcut (e.g., spacebar hold for temporary pan mode).
tasks.testStrategy: Switch to Pan mode. Click a valid conquest target — verify no conquest fires. Drag the map — verify panning works. Switch back to Interaction mode — verify region clicks trigger actions again. Playwright E2E test for mode toggle.

tasks.title: Add Player Box Ability Tooltips (FR-61, US-16)
tasks.description: Player info boxes do not show race and power ability descriptions on hover. Add tooltips to the player dashboard boxes that display the active race and power special abilities. References: FR-61, US-16.
tasks.details: Add pointer-over event handlers to the player dashboard area in the HUD scene. On hover over a player box, show a tooltip containing the active race ability description and the active power ability description. Use the same text from the RaceDefinition and PowerDefinition data tables used in the combo shop tooltips. Tooltips must appear for both Player 1 and Player 2 dashboards and update when the player selects a new race/power combo.
tasks.testStrategy: Hover over the Player 1 info box and verify a tooltip appears showing the race ability and power ability text. Hover over the Player 2 info box and verify the same. Select a new combo and verify the tooltip updates.

tasks.title: Redraw Region Polygons to Match Reference Map (FR-62)
tasks.description: The current region polygon vertex arrays are approximate and do not accurately reflect the region boundaries in the background map image. Retrace all polygons in map2p.ts to match the reference map more closely. References: FR-62.
tasks.details: Using src/assets/reference/2-player-map.jpeg as the reference, retrace polygon vertices for all regions in src/game/data/map2p.ts. Each polygon should follow the visible border lines in the map image. After retracing, verify: adjacency relationships remain symmetric and correct, isEdge and isCoastal flags are still accurate, region center points are updated to fall within the new polygons, and all map data tests still pass. Consider using a browser devtools overlay or a canvas drawing tool to trace coordinates precisely.
tasks.testStrategy: Visually overlay the new polygon hit zones on the map image and verify they align with visible borders. Click along region boundaries and verify correct region is activated. Run all map data unit tests to verify adjacency symmetry and required fields.

tasks.title: Phase 2 Full Regression Testing (E2E and Unit)
tasks.description: Run a full regression test suite after all Phase 2 fixes and enhancements are implemented. Write new Playwright E2E tests for Phase 2 features, run the complete suite across all browsers, and fix any regressions before Phase 2 is considered complete.
tasks.details: Write new Playwright E2E tests covering: decline flow (basic, Ghoul exception, Spirit exception), first conquest entry restriction, conquest cost tooltip accuracy, die roll sequencing (die before End Conquest), redeployment left/right-click model, interaction/pan mode toggle, HUD browse mode, and player box tooltips. Run the full test suite: all Phase 1 E2E tests (mainMenu, hvhGame, hvaiGame) plus all new Phase 2 tests across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. Run all Vitest unit tests. Investigate and fix any failures. All tests must pass with 0 failures before Phase 2 is marked complete.
tasks.testStrategy: npx playwright test (full suite, all browsers) with 0 failures. npx vitest run with 0 failures. Document any regressions found and resolved.

tasks.title: Execute Phase 2 E2E Test Suite
tasks.description: Run the full Playwright E2E test suite and Vitest unit tests to validate all Phase 2 changes. Write any missing E2E tests for new Phase 2 features (first-conquest amber glow, die result display, left/right-click redeployment, pan mode toggle, ability tooltips, updated region polygons). Execute across all browsers (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit) and fix any failures.
tasks.details: 1. Run existing Playwright E2E tests: npx playwright test (all browsers). 2. Run Vitest unit tests: npx vitest run. 3. Write new E2E tests covering Phase 2 features if not already covered by task 18. 4. Fix any test failures or regressions. 5. All tests must pass with 0 failures.
tasks.testStrategy: npx playwright test --reporter=list (all browsers, 0 failures). npx vitest run (0 failures).

tasks.title: Implement Core Game Logic and Visual Bug Fixes
tasks.description: Address critical visual and game rule bugs identified in Phase 1. This includes fixing map viewport clipping, HUD interaction passthrough, initial camera zoom, tooltip scaling, decline flow, first conquest entry rules, conquest cost calculation, and reinforcement die flow sequencing.
tasks.details: Map Image Viewport Clipping: Adjust Board scene camera/container sizing to ensure full map visibility, including turn 8, 9, 10 markers. Race & Power HUD Interaction Passthrough: Implement pointer event capture for the HUD to disable map interactions (hover, click, tooltips) while the HUD is open. Initial Camera Zoom Level: Set the Board scene camera's initial zoom to the maximum zoom-out level. Recalculate region hit polygon scaling to maintain accuracy. Tooltip Zoom Scaling: Refactor tooltip rendering to use screen-space coordinates, ensuring constant visual size regardless of camera zoom. Decline Flow: Wire up the Decline button to appear at the correct turn phase (after ready troops, during or after conquest), invoke the existing applyDecline() engine function, and trigger the full decline animation (banner flip to gray, token reduction, power badge removal). Handle Spirit and Ghoul exceptions correctly. First Conquest Entry Rule Enforcement: Modify getLegalActions() to restrict first conquest targets to border or coastal regions when the player has no occupied regions. Ensure Halflings and Flying power correctly bypass this restriction. Conquest Cost Calculation and Tooltip: Update calculateConquestCost() to correctly compute: 2 (base) + 1 per Mountain token + 1 per Encampment + 1 per Fortress + 1 per Troll's Lair + 1 per Lost Tribe token + 1 per enemy race token present. Update the conquest tooltip to display this computed cost. Reinforcement Die Flow Sequencing: Reorder conquest phase UI so that when the player has at least 1 token remaining but cannot afford a standard conquest, the reinforcement die roll option is the primary action presented. The End Conquest button should only appear after the player has declined the die roll or after the die has been rolled.
tasks.testStrategy: Map Viewport: Visually verify the bottom of the map (including turn 8, 9, 10 markers) is accessible after zooming/panning. Playwright E2E test to verify map renders at full height. HUD Passthrough: Open the Race & Power HUD, hover over HUD options, verify no map tooltips appear and no map regions respond to input. Initial Zoom: Start a new game and verify the entire map is visible without panning or zooming. Verify region hit zones are accurate at default zoom. Tooltip Scaling: Zoom in and out while hovering over a region; verify tooltip appearance is identical at all zoom levels. Decline Flow: Play through a turn and successfully put a race in decline. Verify tokens reduce to 1 per region, banner grays out, power badge is removed. Verify Spirit and Ghoul exceptions work correctly. Playwright E2E test for basic decline flow. First Conquest: Start a game, verify only border/coastal regions are highlighted as valid first conquest targets. Verify non-border non-coastal regions cannot be clicked. Verify Halflings can conquer anywhere. Conquest Cost: Hover over regions with different combinations of defenders and terrain modifiers; verify tooltip shows the correct cost for each. Conquest attempt with insufficient tokens must be rejected. Die Flow: Reach the point in conquest where only 1 token remains; verify the die roll option appears before End Conquest. Verify End Conquest is still accessible if the player chooses not to roll.

tasks.title: Implement UX Enhancements, Map Data Refinement, and Full Regression Testing
tasks.description: Enhance player experience through improved UI feedback, interaction models, and information display. This includes adding text labels and tooltips to HUD elements, refining map interaction modes, updating map region data, and conducting a full regression test suite.
tasks.details: Race and Power Names as Text Labels: Add text labels showing the race name and power name to each combo slot in the shop and to the active player dashboard. These text labels must be visually clear and legible at all zoom levels. Race and Power Ability Tooltips to HUD Combos: Add hover tooltips to each race/power combo in the shop that display the race's special ability description and the power's special ability description, using existing data tables. Also ensure tooltips appear on the player's active race banner and power badge. Allow Browsing Combo HUD During Any Turn Phase: Add a persistent button or control that allows players to open the combo shop HUD in a read-only browse mode at any time during their turn. The HUD must clearly indicate it is in browse-only mode. Highlight First-Conquest Eligible Regions Distinctly: When a player begins their very first conquest (no regions currently owned), highlight border and coastal regions with a distinct visual treatment that differs from the standard valid-target highlight. tasks.title: Execute Full E2E Test Suite and Resolve All Failures
tasks.description: Run the complete Playwright E2E test suite (all Phase 1 and Phase 2 tests) across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit using `npx playwright test`. Investigate any failures using traces, screenshots, and debug mode. Fix all failing tests — whether the failure is in the test code or in the application code. Re-run until the full suite passes with 0 failures across all browsers. Additionally, ensure `npx vitest run` passes with 0 failures.
tasks.details:
1. Execute the full Playwright E2E test suite using the command `npx playwright test`. Ensure the Playwright configuration (`playwright.config.ts`) is set up to run tests across all target browsers: Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit. If not, explicitly run for each project or configure them.
2. For any failing test, utilize Playwright's debugging capabilities:
    - Generate and review test traces (`npx playwright show-report`) to understand the sequence of actions and state changes.
    - Analyze automatically captured screenshots and videos for visual cues of failure.
    - Run tests in debug mode (`PWDEBUG=1 npx playwright test <test-file>`) to step through the test execution and inspect the page state.
3. Based on the investigation, determine if the failure is due to:
    - An issue in the E2E test code (e.g., incorrect selector, outdated assertion, timing issue). Fix the test code accordingly.
    - A bug in the application's Phase 2 implementation. Document the bug, report it to the development team, and implement the necessary application code fix.
4. After implementing fixes, re-run the specific failing tests, then the entire suite, until all tests pass consistently across all three browsers.
5. As a final verification step, execute `npx vitest run` to ensure that all unit tests also pass with 0 failures, confirming overall code stability.
